tips.comment: Kientzheim comes here for the famous green and gold. It is well fancied in this and fairly unexposed. Any market support would be interesting, but I fancy the Henderson team to get one here.
The selection finished well when running on into third last time out. Soceleur looks fairly unexposed and can go close in this one.

Only made hurdles debut in January but had rattled off a hatrick after making a debut 5th at Huntingdon and looks the least exposed in here. Good ground suits and holds a few of these and though reopposing stablemate John Barbour is unexposed too this one is on the upgrade rapidly. Stiff track a slight concern but has won over further and comes here on a real roll. Definite player here and can go close.

Where Red and Blue look to have an each-way chance at a big price in this handicap. He went very well at this track in the Imperial Cup last time, and with a slightly more patient ride, could run into a place.

This race, a Class 2 handicap hurdle, has a really wide open feel to it. An outsider, low in the handicap, is probably the way to go. Fasol is interesting with Harry Skelton (SR 21%) booked for Paul Nicholls. Nicely bred six year-old by Galileo and the dam ran in the Arc. Some of this winter's form over hurdles since joining the yard puts Fasol in with a big shout. Things haven't gone quite to plan but returned from wind surgery with a good winning display at Taunton early in March before being turned over at long odds on last time in a race he should have won. This race, however, is feasibly more the real target. Carries 11 stone off a good handicap mark of 115 and has ability if he can put it all together.

Nardaran was well beaten, finishing only 6th by St Pancras at Musselburgh. However, he showed much better form last time at Taunton on good to firm going, coming away in the straight to win by eleven lengths. Harry Cobden deserts him for Sorceleur, but Sean Bowen is a good replacement, and the juvenile could beat his elders off bottom weight.

Although seemingly against weaker opposition, he has run and won at Class 1 level and nicked 2nd place in a Grade 2 contest over this trip. Strong front-running presence and Kevin Brogan retains the ride. Could well have more progression in him at 4 years old and impossible to rule out at odds this high.

Two wins and a runner-up spot from five starts over hurdles. Won a class two at Cheltenham over a slightly longer trip in December. Decent effort last time out when finishing in mid-division in the Fred Winter at last month's Cheltenham Festival. Looks a massive price for each-way purposes now dropping back down in class and with no concerns about today's underfoot conditions.

Classic Anthem showed improved form to win comfortably over course and distance last time. He could follow up here if he can outbattle the other improving hold-up horse, Eyed Up, in the home straight.
In good form of late when chasing over 2m 4f. With Dan Skelton chasing top trainer, and with Willie having no runner declared here, I think the Skeltons have a great chance.
Inedit Star ran well at Aintree when 6 lengths behind San Bruit, and he has had time to recover from that effort. Getting weight from 6 of his opponents. NAP

Gaelic Warrior is class but unpredictable, and I can't get away from the thinking Pic D'Orhy is suited by flat tracks, so happy to pass both over. Le Patron has saved his best for Sandown, making all to win a novice handicap here by 10L and then following up by claiming the Grade 1 Henry VIII Novice Chase on heavy ground. Rhythm is so vital around here as the jumping can really be tested, and with the cheekpieces fitted, I wouldn't be surprised to see him bounce off from the front to put the rest under pressure. The yard is in good form, and he seems unlikely to be inconvenienced by the quick ground, having won a handicap earlier this season by 7L on good to soft from a mark of 146. Bare form leaves him plenty to find with the market principals, but unlike them, he's proven at the track and can spring a small surprise.

Won first 2 starts for Willie Mullins including a Grade 3 at Gowran Park and ran well when 5th in a grade 1 at Aintree last time out. Likely to be better suited by this drop back in trip to 2m5f down in class.

It was heart in mouth time when this one made a howler at Cheltenham but he still showed his class to be a battling second to Marine Nationale who had more than a helping hand from someone more powerful than a jockey!!! Is unbeaten away from Cheltenham and is chasing a fourth win in this and must be the bet here. Plenty looked over the hill, might prefer softer going or out of their depth so come on Jonbon let's go. Won so well at Aintree last time Cheltenham blip is forgotten and I love course form here so as he's unbeaten around the track looks a good thing to me.
Il Etait Temps doesn't get the credit he deserves. He won last time out, beating a lot of good horses, and he will go close this time.

Harpers Brook is a talented individual who unfortunately has his own ideas about the game. Hopefully, if they go a good gallop, which seems likely, he can run up the hill and grab some place money at huge odds.

Ten of the 20 runners are trained by Willie Mullins. It looks a fun contest but the betting market seems to have it covered. Danny Mullins will be an asset once again to last year's winner Minella Cocooner. The presence of Grangeclare West means that despite an official rating 4lbs higher than last year the 9yo actually carries 4 pounds less (Nick Rockett third in this race last year). Ran well in the National (not beaten far) and conditions (shorter trip; firmer ground) suit better today. A contender.

Was a surprise winner of this last year but that looked a strong event and though hasn't set the world alight this year is slipping to a good mark. Is 4lb higher now but caught the eye last time staying on well in a hot handicap at Aintree. Good ground suits and sure this has been the aim all season. Must go close.
I've been relying on too many MTF notes lately, which have let me down big-style, but I'm quite happy to nap Rahiebb.

This Sea The Moon gelding comes from a strong lineage, with his dam being a winner and a half-sister to the accomplished Voice Of Leader, who excelled up to a mile and a quarter. Under the expert guidance of Andrew Balding and with in-form jockey Jason Watson aboard, this 3-year-old is set to impress. At 22/1, an each-way bet offers great value.

Myal, a 4yo colt by Al Kazeem out of a Dubai Destination mare, finished last season with four straight wins. Well backed into joint favourite for the Spring Mile at Newbury. Ran well there, hitting the front two out and looking the winner only to wander late on. Thunder Roar took the honours but Myal meets that rival on 4lbs better terms now and the drop back to seven furlongs should help. Strongly backed once again. From bottom of the handicap, Myal appeals at odds of 7-2.

English Oak ran some very good races last season but fell away near the end. He could start off on the front foot today as he has been found a great little race for his season debut. Top jockey Tom is on board today. I expect a big run today.

The stable has won this race in the past, and this one brings lots of good form to the table. If he arrives here fit and ready to go after a break, he should hopefully leave his disappointing run at Ascot (7f) on soft ground in a Class 2 Handicap in October last year, when he finished a well-beaten 12th of 18 to 'Volterra', well behind. Now back on better ground, with 'Gorak' at bigger odds, a huge danger.
Yorkshire has had some cracking runs with three wins out of four runs since September, including a C2, and could continue this improvement now returning to turf.
This horse tends to run his best races in the early part of the season. Has run well here in the past and looks fairly handicapped at an attractive each way price

There's a lot of horses being backed in this, Telemark on the other hand is friendless in the early market but he looks good value to me at 20/1. The 4yo was even sent off as short as 2/1 for a Group 3 in his 2yo days, and he looks one of only a very few in the race that looks capable of winning off their current mark. The trainer/jockey have won 3 of their last 6 together and 7 furlongs is clearly his trip.

This horse normally comes on for his first run of the season. Has won here in the past and after having a run should be ready to put his best foot forward. He is a huge price which underestimates his ability.
Not in the best of form, but should welcome the dropped mark with only 2lb above the last winning mark. Makes course debut tomorrow but has a chance given his ability.

Returned after a 160-day break to take 2nd at Leicester towards the beginning of the month for a new yard. Solid form seems to be at Yarmouth, but no reason to show further improvement here for a new trainer.
Roland Garros looks an interesting prospect for the Gosden camp. Looked like they needed the run on reappearance and can go close here under a nice weight.
I really like the look of this horse today. It was very unlucky last time out with no run and lost by only 5 lengths. Good strong jockey on today, so I'm on each way for a big run.

This horse runs his best races here, and the shrewd trainer clearly means business now that he's gone to the trouble of booking Rossa Ryan on the horse for the first time. The trainer has had the horse for 7 runs and only now has decided to race him over turf, which is where his latest runs have been. The horse's last win was, in fact, over a similar trip and ground just over a year ago off 74, and he's down to 63 now, so his chances are fairly obvious.
Showed solid form last season in similar handicaps. She should have a race in her off this mark, and low tends to be the place that you want to be on this sprint track.

Belsito won at Redcar as a juvenile and again at Carlisle last June. He finished last season with two narrow defeats at Redcar, and if a recent wind operation results in any improvement, he looks a good each-way bet with 5 places on offer.

Top stable and has stable jockey on board today, so a big run is expected. Below par last time, but the top jockey wasn't on board. If you go on best form, should be thrown in a race that will take a lot to win.

Has a good record over this distance and last time out won at Bath over 5 furlongs. The new trainer's horses are in good form of late and run off a fair mark with a 3lb claimer on board. Good EW chance.

Ship trip fitter from last run and has run in hot races last year at this trip on this ground and with Jo Mason booked, which I thought was interesting as she usually ride for the Fahay team. I think she is overpriced as a filly. Potentially, that is why she's at the price as up against the boys, but she could hold her own.

Lady Diesel has not quite kicked on since her debut but she was well backed last time and might just be working her way back to form. Still a bit to find but no shock if she shows more today with conditions looking fine.

This horse was given an easy ride first time out, and it went into my tracker straight away. With the stable jockey for the owners onboard today, Havlin can win this race, which can be a prep for better races this season and next.
Bintalina shaped well last time out and looked like they needed the run. They should have come on for the run and can get their head in front here from a good draw.
Carron won nicely on reappearance and looked like there was plenty more to come. Goes here on a very nice weight. Looking unexposed, can go in again.

William Haggas places horses with a profile like the selection with great skill, and this 3yo Sea The Stars colt will have come on from his pipe-opener at the Craven meeting, where he didn’t act on the undulations at HQ. However, he ran well enough here over C&D last October on his second racecourse start. The yard has a near 30% strike rate here at Haydock, and he's now 2lbs down to 80 from 82. As we know, he'll prefer this flat track. He's worth a shot.
I believe this horse has lots of potential but found the effort at York challenging when 11th of 11 last August. Dropping down 4 classes could be significant if he is in top form.
Stardinia 2 year old bay filly. Drawn 1 which could be an advantage in this 17 runner race. The stables 2 year olds have started the season well so might be worth a small wager.
Coppull, a 2-year-old bay colt. A Bated Breath colt with Clive Cox looks a likely type on pedigree. Nice each-way price.

Mighty Vega, on debut, finished 5th in what was a large field of 17 horses. Really finished that race well. Second race in, definitely going to be closer after what looked to be an impressive run on debut.

Ran on well to take the spoils last time out at Beverley over five furlongs. Has won over today's longer trip. Up four pounds for that last win but looks a big player here with top young jockey Billy Loughnane taking the ride. Another positive.

None of these particularly stand out as an obvious choice, and all have questions to answer. For this lad, the ground is the concern as his successes have come on slower ground, but his failings on quicker have also come without Oisin in the saddle. A front runner, and he will need to be from stall 11. He needs the unopposed lead that he should get on paper and to get over as much as he can. Small stake.

Been running well recently, but took a nice victory at Southwell on the all-weather after a gelding op and a 146-day break. Tends to be much better on a 2nd run after a return, and should strip fitter here despite a 6lb rise.

Looks a very competitive race, and I'm very interested to see this one dropping back in trip for a very shrewd stable. They are starting to turn out winners, and if coping with the drop back in trip, it may be worth a look after finishing a cracking 3rd of 17 to 'Myal' at Doncaster (7f 6yds) on soft ground in what was a very competitive Class 3 Handicap in October last year. It returns on a 1lb lower mark and seems to act on any ground, so could surprise.

Commanche Falls is played in a slightly optimistic spirit. Achieved a string of three victories at Pattern level in the summer of 2023. Ran some good races last year, a second place to Believing at Listed level and ran sixth in the Ayr Gold Cup off OR107. Happier on good ground and conditions here should suit. Has run ok on first outings in the past - fair effort in the Abernant last year. Still just eight years old but slightly better handicapped these days on a mark of 103. 12 wins from 45 starts on turf. Trainer Michael Dods has had a couple of recent winners. Possibilities at double-figure odds in an 11-runner Class 2 sprint.

Rousing Encore is bottom weight here but ran well enough first time out when just a head behind Havana Pusey at Newbury. Both finished well from behind in 4th and 5th, and Leicester could suit both horses better, with Rousing Encore likely to improve for his first run since December.

Trainer Charlie Appleby and Godolphin have just the two runners anywhere today, and they are both in the same race. Jockey William Buick has only the one ride, Naval Command, which he chose over Urban Warrior (respected). The well-bred, expensive, Lope De Vega 3-year-old colt out of All At Sea (Sea The Stars) was held up in the rear of midfield, outpaced, and pushed along passing halfway. He rallied from 1f out and kept on to finish 4th on debut in a hot maiden over a mile at Kempton. Upped to 10f here should really suit, and I expect him to do the biz on his seasonal debut.
Skimmer has the benefit of a run and did well, finishing third. With that run under their belt, they can go a couple better and win this in what should be a good race.

One of 3 runners for Tony Carroll in this race. Douglas DC gave himself a mountain to climb when fluffing the start at Wolverhampton on last run, but was impressive when managing to stay on for a 3rd place finish. Finished 2nd here previously, only beaten a length. Despite remaining a maiden on the flat after 17 runs, he managed to win over obstacles for Gordon Elliott. The trainer has hit form of late and it should be a matter of time before getting the first win on turf from a low handicap mark.

Twilight Romance pulled too hard at Newmarket but still has some solid form in the book and the drop back down in grade should help a lot. With a top jockey booked he looks set to be bang there if settling better early.
Will strip fitter for a run over a furlong further 13 days ago following an absence of 7 months and the drop in trip will suit.
A beaten favourite in two runs from three for new yard, most recently over a mile at Yarmouth earlier this month. Interesting trying this 6 furlong trip for the first time.

Pembrokeshire has not been great since changing yards and has been a bit duff on all runs on the AW. But I think the return to turf with a mark 10 lbs below his last win in July will see him back in the game. I would have put him in for the win, but I am not so sure about the drop to 6f, hence EW 4P.

Still a maiden after 19 runs and did not look any closer to ending the barren run last time out when 11th of 11. But it has course experience and continues to drop down the weights, which just might be enough to cause a shock tomorrow.

Will be looking for good things from this horse for the new yard. It will need to make improvements from the LTO effort at Wolverhampton at the start of this month. But sometimes, a switch from AW to turf can be beneficial.

Surrey Belle was a bit keen at Kelso but her overall profile is solid and she had a good 2024 on the Flat. She likes to get on with it and if settling better back on the level she should be right there at the finish.
Diamand de Vindecy won on reappearance and looks fairly unexposed. Needs a career-best to win this, but off a lovely low mark here, can go close.

ZIMMERMAN is 1lb lower than when reappearing for this race last season. He ran with credit that day and this strong northern yard may be in better form and their runner seen to better effect this time around. He has taken in deeper races through his career and with this a potential early target he appeals.

Most likely to be prominent/lead, which suits Ripon. Race fit. Won over CD by 3.25L off 80, so 82 shouldn't be too far of a stretch and has run well up to 88/89. 6yo now, with the 5/6-year-olds always performing better at this stage in the season before the 4yo reach peak maturity. Ground fine and should run a nice race.

Makes debut for the James Owen yard. Not yet fired in the UK but has won three times on turf. Went off fancied when last seen, so must have shown something. No surprise if making a winning start for the yard.

The Barron yard are in fine form at this early stage of the season, and Pilgrim might be up to winning on seasonal debut. He was the very smart winner of the three year-old sprint handicap at Royal Ascot last year, and he should be able to develop into an even better older horse.

Manila Scouse last won in August when running off an 83. Then returned from a break at the start of this month and was pants, but will be all the better for that run. He is just 2 lbs above that last winning mark and has Amie on top claiming 3 lbs, so I expect more today.
Has six wins to his name and his mark has dropped to a level where he can be competitive again here.

Stockpyle was a close second off a 73 on GD in March when second up for a new yard. While not so good last time out, I think the return to 1 mile today, having won at this trip last year, could be enough to get to the top step.

This is a very open affair where stakes should be controlled firmly. Pisanello ran quite well to be third here on his first run of the year and will doubtless strip fitter this time. He has some very strong form in these northern handicaps, and at 10/1, deserves to carry a little investment.

Invitorio is improving with each run and that Pontefract effort was a strong piece of form. He is learning all the time and looks to have been found a good opportunity here to keep the momentum going.

Macedonian makes only his second appearance on turf. He made his debut in a Newmarket maiden last year, with a very good second-place finish behind the easy winner who holds a 2,000 Guineas entry. Since then, he has only raced on the AW, getting off the mark on his penultimate run with a last-stride victory at Kempton. He failed to back that up next time but was drawn wide. The trainer's only runner here today, and the stable has an excellent record at Ripon, with a 31% winning strike rate overall at the track and a 50% strike rate over this CD.

Ziggy’s Ariel enjoyed a solid campaign last year, securing two victories from six starts, with her most recent win coming over 6 furlongs at Wolverhampton in November. She made a promising seasonal return on the all-weather surface, finishing fourth out of eight in a competitive handicap at the same track three weeks ago, showing she has retained her form. A consistent performer with a sharp turn of foot, she now switches back to turf??'a surface she has handled well in the past??'and is one to keep an eye on in her current shape.

Berkshire Phantom was supported last time and ran ok without landing a blow, but his best efforts have come on the AW. Up in trip today and needs to find a bit more, but if he settles better he could sneak into it.
Makes turf debut. Won on AW when last seen in February, value for extra as she ran wide and had to overcome pace bias. Goes up 4lb and should follow up if transferring form over to turf.

Tarlac has been running consistently and that Newcastle fourth was solid enough. He’s on a fair mark based on his AW form and with the yard going well he should give a good account if he handles the quicker ground.
On their last effort, Kinswoman looked like there was better to come, and this could be their chance. They have to be respected in this one.

6:25pm ??' Doncaster (NAP) Oriental Prince ??' 10/1 (Each Way) Oriental Prince looks a solid each-way play here. He steps back into a Class 3 handicap after an eye-catching effort in a Class 2 at Musselburgh over 7f, where he finished a close 4th, just 2.5 lengths off the winner. That was a huge run, especially considering the trip may have stretched him. Prior to that, he landed a Class 6 contest and was unbeaten in his three starts over 6f, showing serious consistency. Back over his ideal trip and down in grade, he looks primed to go close. With Paul Mulrennan back on board who guided him to three wins, everything points to a big run. Good luck
Makes turf debut having had 3 runs on AW, winning last time. Prior to that win, had run very green in 2 previous races. Learning by the race and should have plenty more to offer.
Has an each-way chance if fit enough on return. Won on nursery debut on penultimate start before getting outclassed in a French race. Makes reappearance here after 7 months off.
A change of trainer, now with Jim Goldie. She performed well under Jardine, and I can't see why she cannot continue doing so. Still well treated and has a good stall draw in 6 this evening.
Quite a few course specialist types here, but Dandy Dinmont looks the main danger to them all off this mark with Faye Mcmannomen up today. It loves the course, unlike me!
Has won six times previously over this distance and the 2 lbs increase for his latest win at Nottingham might not be enough to stop him going in again here.

This horse is 1 from 2 over C&D and loves this fast ground. The trainer's runners are going better now than the bare form would suggest, and the horse has run well after a break before. He's tumbled down the handicap to just 68 now, and at this time last year, he was going down by a length off a mark of 80. That C&D win was off 80 too, and he clearly has the ability to go close off this mark.

Glendown has won 5 times in his career and is interesting here off the same mark as his last turf win at Pontefract last August. He also won at Southwell in November and was second, beaten just 0.5 lengths on return to turf at Leicester three weeks ago. He looks a good each way bet here.

Toptime ran a decent race last time out over this course and distance, finishing just 2.5 lengths off the winner in 6th. That was a solid effort from a middle draw in a big field. This time, he’s drawn wide, but that should actually help him, as he likes to race up near the front and get across to the rail early. Lewis Edmunds is back in the saddle, the same jockey who rode him to victory at Southwell, and Toptime has already won over this track and trip before. If he gets out well, he could be right in the mix. Good Luck!

Has a poor strike rate but is capable from this mark, winning off 59 last July and running well on reappearance run on AW last time. Beaten in a photo having raced too close to a strong pace. EW chance.
Carrados showed plenty of promise last summer and that Goodwood second reads well. Trainer is firing and if he handles the AW and is straight enough after the layoff he looks a serious player here.

This lightly-raced maiden finished 8th out of 9 in a handicap at this course 3 weeks ago. There is room for improvement, and trainer David Simcock, who has achieved 40 victories and 121 places here in the past 5 seasons, is likely to have a solid strategy in place. With a jockey on board who has a 7lb claim, making an each-way bet at 22/1 a promising opportunity.
